meta: You asked AI for a logo and love it, but is that logo really yours under copyright? In many countries copyright only protects what people create.

muc.title: An AI logo: whose is it?
muc.text: Mark asks AI to draw a logo for his café, loves it, and wants to know whether the logo belongs to him under copyright.

muc.title: The law needs a human author
muc.text: Bit explains: in many countries, like the US, copyright only protects what a person creates. An image made entirely by AI from one prompt is usually hard to protect, so other people may reuse it.

muc.title: Heavy editing changes things
muc.text: If you use AI for a draft, then redraw and edit a lot yourself, your creative part has a chance to be protected. Laws differ by country and are changing, so for big projects, ask a lawyer.

muc.title: Don't copy others
muc.text: The bigger risk is copying others: asking AI to draw a famous cartoon character or another brand's logo to sell products can break their copyright.

muc.title: Read the tool's terms
muc.text: Before using AI images for business, read the terms of the tool you use and check whether commercial use is allowed.

muc.title: Keep a record of your process
muc.text: Next time you make images for work, save the prompt, the drafts and the versions you edited yourself. That's proof of your creative part.
